title: NCL Mine Surveyor Mock 07
pattern: 100 MCQs, 100 marks, 90 min, NO negative marking

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'apparent dip' of a bed in any direction other than the true dip direction is always:
questions.solution: The apparent dip in any direction other than the true dip direction is always less than the true dip.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A geological map showing 'strike and dip' symbols with the dip angle increasing in one direction indicates:
options: A uniformly dipping bed or the limb of a fold
questions.solution: Consistently increasing dip angles in one direction indicate a uniformly dipping bed or one limb of a fold.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In mineral deposit studies, a 'contact' on a geological map refers to:
options: The meeting point of two survey stations
The surface where two different rock types meet
The boundary of the mining lease
questions.solution: A contact is the surface or boundary where two different rock types or formations meet.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When traversing steep topography, the main challenge is:
options: Large differences in elevation between stations making direct sighting difficult
questions.solution: Steep topography creates large elevation differences between stations, making direct sighting and measurement challenging.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'auxiliary telescope' in traversing is used to:
options: Overcome obstacles by providing an intermediate sighting point
questions.solution: An auxiliary telescope (subtense bar or auxiliary instrument) provides intermediate sighting points to overcome obstacles in steep terrain.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The curvature and refraction correction for a vertical distance is given by the formula (approximately):
questions.solution: The curvature and refraction correction in metres is approximately 0.0673D² where D is the distance in kilometres.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In reciprocal levelling between two points A and B, the true difference in height is obtained by:
options: Taking readings from both positions (near A and near B) and averaging the differences
Taking readings from one instrument position only
questions.solution: Reciprocal levelling eliminates errors due to curvature, refraction, and collimation error by averaging readings from two instrument positions.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When traversing in steep terrain, the 'reduced observation' method involves:
options: Taking fewer observations to save time
Reducing slope measurements to horizontal and vertical components
questions.solution: Reduced observations involve converting slope measurements to horizontal and vertical components using trigonometric reductions.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The effect of curvature of the earth on levelling readings makes distant objects appear:
options: To the left of their true position
questions.solution: Earth's curvature causes distant objects to appear lower than their actual position when viewed from a level line.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As per DGMS Circular 2/2010, strata and dump slope monitoring is mandatory for dumps exceeding ______ in height.
questions.solution: DGMS Circular 2/2010: monitoring (including slope stability radar / real-time monitoring) is made mandatory for dumps exceeding 60 m height.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: DGMS (Tech.) (S&T) Circular No. 02 of 2010 deals with:
options: Design, control and monitoring of pit and dump slopes in opencast mines
questions.solution: DGMS (Tech.) (S&T) Circular No. 02 dated 06.07.2010 concerns design, control and monitoring of pit and dump slopes in opencast mines.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When the line of sight is inclined upwards in tachymetry, the horizontal distance is:
options: Stadia interval × stadia constant × cos²(vertical angle)
Stadia interval × stadia constant × tan(vertical angle)
Stadia interval × stadia constant × sin(vertical angle)
questions.solution: For an inclined line of sight, horizontal distance = KS cos²α where K is the stadia constant, S is the stadia interval, and α is the vertical angle.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'stadia constant' (multiplying constant) for a standard tachymeter is:
questions.solution: The standard stadia multiplying constant for a tachymeter with the stadia hairs equally spaced is 100.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In traversing steep terrain, 'vertical curvature correction' is important because:
options: It has no effect on survey measurements
It causes systematic errors in elevation measurements that increase with distance
It affects only the horizontal angle measurements
questions.solution: Vertical curvature (combined with refraction) causes systematic errors in elevation that increase with the square of the distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'profile levelling' along a steep slope is used to determine:
options: The vertical cross-section showing elevation changes along a route
questions.solution: Profile levelling determines the vertical cross-section of the ground along a specified route, showing elevation changes.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When sighting a staff held at a lower level than the instrument in tachymetry, the vertical angle is:
questions.solution: When the staff is at a lower level, the line of sight is inclined downward, giving a negative (depression) vertical angle.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As per the Mines Rescue Rules 1985, a rescue station shall be under the charge of a Superintendent assisted by at least:
options: 2 instructors and a rescue brigade of at least 18 rescue-trained persons
questions.solution: MRR 1985: a rescue station has a Superintendent, at least 2 instructors and a rescue brigade of at least 18 rescue-trained persons.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In steep topography, the 'contouring' method helps in:
options: Representing the three-dimensional terrain on a two-dimensional map
questions.solution: Contouring represents the three-dimensional terrain surface on a two-dimensional map using lines of equal elevation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The curvature correction for a distance of 5 km is approximately:
questions.solution: Curvature correction = 0.0673 × D² = 0.0673 × 5² = 0.0673 × 25 ≈ 1.68 m.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When traversing steep slopes, the 'reduction' of slope measurements to horizontal involves:
options: Adding the slope distance to the vertical distance
Dividing the slope distance by the sine of the slope angle
Multiplying the slope distance by the cosine of the slope angle
Multiplying the slope distance by the tangent of the slope angle
questions.solution: Horizontal distance = slope distance × cos(slope angle). This reduces the slope measurement to its horizontal component.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'auxiliary station' in steep terrain traversing is established to:
options: Provide an intermediate point for sighting when direct line of sight is obstructed
questions.solution: Auxiliary stations provide intermediate sighting points when the direct line of sight between main stations is obstructed by terrain.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'refraction coefficient' for ordinary atmospheric conditions is approximately:
questions.solution: The average refraction coefficient for ordinary conditions is approximately 0.13, meaning refraction bends the line of sight toward the earth.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A shot-firer who has not been employed in blasting duties for more than 6 months shall undergo:
options: Retraining in the handling of explosives before resuming such duties
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 13: retraining in handling of explosives is required after an absence from such duties exceeding 6 months.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When the staff is vertical but the line of sight is inclined at angle α to the horizontal, the correct horizontal distance is:
questions.solution: For a vertical staff with an inclined line of sight, horizontal distance = L × cos²α, where L is the stadia reading.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'traverse in steep terrain' should be plotted using:
options: Both horizontal coordinates (northing, easting) and reduced levels
questions.solution: A traverse in steep terrain should include both horizontal coordinates and reduced levels for complete three-dimensional positioning.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'reciprocal observation' method for curvature and refraction correction requires:
options: Simultaneous observations from both ends of the line
Observations at different times of day
questions.solution: Reciprocal observations are made simultaneously from both ends of the line to cancel out curvature and refraction effects.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In steep topography, the 'offset' method of surveying involves:
options: Taking perpendicular measurements from a main survey line to features on either side
questions.solution: Offsets are perpendicular measurements taken from a main survey line (chain line or traverse line) to locate features on either side.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: CAD software in mine surveying is primarily used for:
options: Preparation, editing, and maintenance of mine plans and sections
questions.solution: CAD (Computer-Aided Design) software is the primary tool for digital preparation, editing, and maintenance of mine plans and sections.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A Digital Terrain Model (DTM) represents:
options: A three-dimensional mathematical representation of the ground surface
questions.solution: A DTM is a digital representation of the ground surface, created from survey data points, showing the three-dimensional terrain.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: 3D laser profiling of mine surfaces involves:
options: Using laser scanning to capture detailed three-dimensional surface geometry
questions.solution: 3D laser profiling uses laser scanning technology to capture high-density three-dimensional point data of mine surfaces.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: GIS (Geographic Information System) in mining is used for:
options: Integration, analysis, and visualization of spatial data from multiple sources
questions.solution: GIS integrates multiple spatial datasets, enabling complex analysis, overlay operations, and visualization for mine planning and management.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The primary advantage of computer-based mine planning over manual methods is:
options: It eliminates the need for surveyors
Faster processing, easy modifications, and accurate volume calculations
questions.solution: Computer-based methods offer faster data processing, easy editing/modifications, accurate calculations, and efficient storage and retrieval.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'grid model' in DTM for mine surveying involves:
options: Dividing the area into a regular grid and assigning elevation to each grid node
questions.solution: A grid model divides the terrain into a regular grid, with elevation values assigned to each grid intersection point.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Volume calculation using computer methods in opencast mining is done by:
options: Comparing DTMs of different dates or using grid/prism methods
questions.solution: Computer methods compare DTMs from different dates or use grid/prism methods to calculate volumes of excavation or dumping accurately.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'triangulated irregular network' (TIN) in DTM represents terrain using:
options: A network of non-overlapping triangles connecting survey data points
questions.solution: TIN represents terrain as a network of non-overlapping triangles connecting survey data points, adapting to terrain complexity.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In mine plan preparation using CAD, the 'layer' concept is used to:
options: Organize different types of information (geology, workings, contours) on separate overlays
questions.solution: Layers in CAD allow different types of information (geological features, workings, contours, text) to be organized and managed separately.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'Digital Elevation Model' (DEM) differs from a DTM in that:
options: A DEM is always more accurate
A DEM represents only the bare earth surface, while DTM may include features
questions.solution: A DEM represents the bare earth surface without features, while a DTM may include above-ground features like buildings and vegetation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'bench profiling' using computers in opencast mining helps in:
options: Monitoring bench geometry, slope stability, and volumetric changes over time
questions.solution: Computer-based bench profiling enables monitoring of bench geometry, slope stability assessment, and tracking volumetric changes over time.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A rescue-trained person shall practise with breathing apparatus at least:
options: 8 times a year, of which 4 in mines
4 times a year, of which 2 in mines
questions.solution: MRR 1985: rescue-trained persons practise with breathing apparatus at least 8 times a year, including 4 practices in the mine.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'highwall mapping' using computer methods involves:
options: Digital capture and analysis of highwall geometry, geology, and stability
questions.solution: Computer-based highwall mapping involves digital capture and analysis of highwall geometry, geological features, and stability parameters.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A rescue room is required at a mine where the number of persons employed belowground exceeds 100 and:
options: The mine produces less than 100 tonnes a day
There is no rescue station within 35 km
questions.solution: MRR 1985: a rescue room is required when more than 100 persons work belowground and no rescue station is within 35 km.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In mine surveying, 'volumetric analysis' using computers is important for:
options: Estimating quantities of excavation, dumping, and coal production
questions.solution: Computer-based volumetric analysis calculates quantities of overburden removed, material dumped, coal produced, and remaining reserves.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'slope stability analysis' using computer software in opencast mining involves:
options: Mathematical modeling of slope geometry, material properties, and failure mechanisms
questions.solution: Computer-based slope stability analysis uses mathematical models (limit equilibrium, finite element) to assess slope safety factors.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The advantage of using GIS over CAD for mine planning is:
options: GIS is only for underground mines
GIS can perform spatial analysis and integrate multiple data layers with attribute data
questions.solution: GIS offers spatial analysis capabilities, attribute data integration, and complex querying that basic CAD cannot provide.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In computerized mine surveying, 'coordinate transformation' is used to:
options: Convert coordinates between different reference systems or projections
questions.solution: Coordinate transformation converts data between different reference systems (e.g., WGS84 to local grid) or map projections.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'dump profiling' using 3D laser scanning provides:
options: Detailed three-dimensional geometry including volumes, slopes, and surface features
questions.solution: 3D laser scanning of dumps provides detailed geometry including precise volume calculation, slope angles, surface features, and changes over time.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'cross-section generation' from DTM using computers involves:
options: Extracting elevation profiles along any specified line from the digital model
questions.solution: Computer software can automatically generate cross-sections along any specified line by extracting and interpolating elevation data from the DTM.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In mine planning, 'surface modeling' using computers helps in:
options: Creating three-dimensional terrain models for volume calculations and visualization
questions.solution: Surface modeling creates 3D terrain representations for volume calculations, design optimization, and visualization of mine surfaces.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'database management' in computerized mine surveying stores:
options: Survey observations, coordinates, levels, and all related spatial and attribute data
questions.solution: Survey databases store all field observations, computed coordinates, levels, and related data for easy retrieval and analysis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In computerized mine plan preparation, 'symbol libraries' are used to:
options: Ensure consistent representation of standard mining features on plans
questions.solution: Symbol libraries provide standardized symbols for consistent representation of geological features, workings, and other mining elements.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under the Mines Rescue Rules 1985, the breathing apparatus kept at a rescue station or rescue room shall:
options: Be of the same type and make
Be of different types for flexibility
questions.solution: MRR 1985, Rule 11(4): breathing apparatus at a rescue station/room must be of the same type and make for interchangeability.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The water-danger plan maintained under CMR 2017 shows water bodies existing within ______ of the boundary of the mine.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 65(1)(g): a water-danger plan and section show water bodies existing up to 200 m of the mine boundary.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In computerized surveying, 'error detection' capabilities include:
options: Automated flagging of blunders, misclosures, and out-of-range values
questions.solution: Computer software can automatically detect blunders, check misclosures, flag out-of-range values, and identify other survey errors.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'report generation' feature in mine survey software produces:
options: Formatted reports with tables, calculations, and graphics for management and regulatory compliance
questions.solution: Report generation produces formatted documents containing survey data, calculations, maps, and analysis results for various purposes.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'import/export' capability in mine survey software is important for:
options: Exchange of survey data between different software and formats (DXF, CSV, etc.)
questions.solution: Import/export capabilities enable data exchange between different software platforms and file formats, facilitating workflow integration.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The joint survey plan showing workings near the common boundary with an adjacent mine shall be signed by:
options: The surveyors and managers of both the mine and the adjacent mine
Only the surveyor of the mine
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 65(1)(e): the joint survey plan is signed by the surveyor and the manager of the mine and of adjoining mines whose workings come within 60 m of the common boundary.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'time-series analysis' of mine surface data using computers helps in:
options: Tracking changes in mine surfaces over time for stability monitoring and production tracking
questions.solution: Time-series analysis compares surface data from different dates to track changes, monitor stability, and assess production progress.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Every mine plan or section under CMR 2017 shall show:
options: The true north, or the magnetic meridian with the date of the latter
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 64(1)(b): plans show true north or magnetic meridian and the date of the later.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: AutoCAD is widely used in mine surveying for:
options: 2D drafting and design of mine plans, sections, and profiles
questions.solution: AutoCAD is extensively used for 2D drafting and design of mine plans, sections, profiles, and other engineering drawings.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Liscad is a surveying software package that is particularly strong in:
options: Land surveying computations, coordinate geometry, and traversing
questions.solution: Liscad is specialized for land surveying computations including coordinate geometry, traversing, levelling, and area calculations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Autoplotter is used in mine surveying for:
options: Digital terrain modeling, contour generation, and volume calculations
questions.solution: Autoplotter is used for DTM creation, contour generation, volume calculations, and profile plotting from survey data.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: RiScan Pro is the software associated with:
options: 3D terrestrial laser scanners (Riegl scanners) for point cloud processing
questions.solution: RiScan Pro is Riegl's software for processing point cloud data from their 3D terrestrial laser scanners.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In Surpac, a 'digital terrain model' is created by:
options: Triangulating survey points to create a TIN surface
questions.solution: Surpac creates DTM by triangulating survey data points into a Triangulated Irregular Network (TIN) surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'AutoCAD block' feature in mine plan preparation is used to:
options: Create reusable symbols for standard mining features
questions.solution: AutoCAD blocks allow creation of reusable symbols for standard mining features (boreholes, workings, symbols) for consistency.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In Liscad, the 'traverse computation' module performs:
options: Adjustment of traverse observations and computation of coordinates
questions.solution: Liscad's traverse module performs observation adjustment, coordinate computation, and error analysis for survey traverses.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: RiScan Pro's 'registration' process involves:
options: Aligning multiple scans from different positions into a common coordinate system
questions.solution: Registration in RiScan Pro aligns multiple scans from different scanner positions into a unified coordinate system.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In Surpac, 'geological modeling' helps in:
options: Creating three-dimensional models of ore bodies and geological structures
questions.solution: Surpac's geological modeling creates 3D models of ore bodies, coal seams, and geological structures for resource estimation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: AutoCAD's 'layer management' in mine surveying is used to:
options: Organize different types of information for selective display and plotting
questions.solution: Layer management organizes different information types (contours, workings, text, symbols) for selective display, editing, and plotting.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Plans and sections required under CMR 2017 shall be corrected and maintained up-to-date at intervals not exceeding:
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 64(4): plans are kept corrected up-to-date not earlier than 3 months.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Unless otherwise approved, mine plans and sections under CMR 2017 shall be prepared on a scale with a representative factor of:
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 64(1)(d): plans are on a scale with RF 2000:1 or 1000:1, with a scale bar at least 25 cm long.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Surpac's 'survey data management' includes:
options: Import, storage, processing, and export of survey observations and coordinates
questions.solution: Surpac manages survey data through import, storage, processing, and export of field observations, coordinates, and computed results.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In AutoCAD, the 'hatch' command is used in mine plans to:
options: Fill areas with patterns to represent different rock types or features
Measure the area of the hatch pattern
questions.solution: The hatch command fills enclosed areas with patterns to represent different rock types, workings, or other features on mine plans.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Liscad's 'levelling' module is used for:
options: Booking, reduction, and adjustment of levelling observations
questions.solution: Liscad's levelling module handles booking of field observations, reduction of levels, and adjustment for misclosure.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Autoplotter supports import of survey data from:
options: Multiple formats including CSV, DXF, and raw instrument data
questions.solution: Autoplotter imports data from various formats including CSV, DXF, and raw data from total stations and GPS receivers.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In RiScan Pro, 'classification' of point cloud data means:
options: Assigning points to categories (ground, vegetation, buildings, etc.)
Assigning colours to the point cloud
questions.solution: Classification assigns each point in the cloud to categories like ground, vegetation, buildings, or other features for analysis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Surpac's 'mine design' module is used for:
options: Designing pit layouts, haul roads, benches, and dump locations
questions.solution: Surpac's mine design module designs pit layouts, haul roads, bench configurations, dump locations, and other mine infrastructure.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: AutoCAD's 'dimension' tool in mine plans is used to:
options: Add measurements and annotations showing distances, angles, and coordinates
questions.solution: The dimension tool adds measurement annotations showing distances, angles, coordinates, and other dimensions on mine plans.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In Liscad, 'coordinate geometry' (COGO) functions include:
options: Intersection calculations, bearing/distance computations, and area calculations
questions.solution: COGO functions include intersection calculations, bearing/distance computations, coordinate transformations, and area calculations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: RiScan Pro can export point cloud data to:
options: Multiple formats including LAS, LAZ, E57, and ASCII
questions.solution: RiScan Pro exports point cloud data to various industry-standard formats (LAS, LAZ, E57, ASCII) for use in other software.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In Surpac, 'resource estimation' involves:
options: Using geological models and statistical methods to estimate ore/reserve quantities
questions.solution: Resource estimation uses geological models, geostatistical methods (kriging, inverse distance) to estimate ore body quantities and grades.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The average of a committee of 5 members is decreased by 3 years when one member aged 50 years is replaced by a new member. What is the age of the new member?
questions.solution: Total decrease = 5 × 3 = 15. New member age = 50 - 15 = 35

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The price of sugar increases by 25%. By how much percent should a family reduce consumption so that expenditure remains same?
questions.solution: New consumption = (100/125) × old = 80% of old. Reduction = 20%

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: If today is Wednesday, what day will it be after 100 days?
questions.solution: 100 = 14×7 + 2. Wednesday + 2 = Friday

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A good is marked 60% above its cost price. If a discount of 25% is offered, what is the profit percentage?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: PM Fasal Bima Yojana is related to:
questions.solution: PM Fasal Bima Yojana provides crop insurance to farmers.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) envisages investment of how much?
questions.solution: NIP envisages infrastructure investment of ₹111 lakh crore during 2020-2025.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which scheme aims to provide clean drinking water to every household by 2024?
questions.solution: Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide piped water supply to every rural household.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian city hosted the 2017 FIFA U-17 World Cup?
questions.solution: The 2017 FIFA U-17 World Cup was held in Mumbai, Kolkata, New Delhi, and other cities.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who is the first Indian to score a triple century in Test cricket?
questions.solution: Virender Sehwag scored India's first triple century (309) in Test cricket.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Agni missile series belongs to which category?
questions.solution: Agni is a series of medium to intercontinental range ballistic missiles.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian weightlifter won a gold medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games?
questions.solution: Mirabai Chanu won gold in weightlifting at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Tejas aircraft is manufactured by which Indian company?
questions.solution: Tejas (LCA) is manufactured by HAL.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which country will host the 2028 Summer Olympics?
questions.solution: Los Angeles will host the 2028 Summer Olympics.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: India's first aircraft carrier INS Vikrant was commissioned in which year?
questions.solution: INS Vikrant (IAC-1) was commissioned on 2 September 2022.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Neeraj Chopra won Olympic gold in which event?
questions.solution: Neeraj Chopra won gold in javelin throw at Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian state has its own commando force known as 'Garud Commando Force'?
questions.solution: Assam has the Garud Commando Force under Assam Police.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who was the first woman to climb Mount Everest?
questions.solution: Bachendri Pal was the first Indian woman to summit Everest in 1984.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which missile is India's first anti-satellite missile?
questions.solution: Mission Shakti (ASAT) demonstrated India's anti-satellite capability in 2019.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) works under which ministry?
questions.solution: BRO works under the Ministry of Defence.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian badminton player became the first to win an Olympic medal?
questions.solution: Saina Nehwal won a bronze medal at London 2012 Olympics.
